stops.note: Livy complains that after Rome's armies returned from Asia in 187 BC, the cook, once the cheapest slave, became the most costly
in Ælfric's Colloquy (c. 1000), the cook argues that without him the others would have to eat their vegetables raw
the verb came from the noun; Hannah Glasse's best-selling The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy appeared in 1747

current_meaning: to prepare food by heating; a person who prepares food
